phenotypes.label: Cardiometabolic comorbidity with pain/fatigue
phenotypes.description: Chronic cardiometabolic conditions dominate, led by essential hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Patients also have a nonspecific symptom burden with chronic pain, fatigue, headaches, low back and chest pain, alongside obesity, coronary atherosclerosis, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease.

phenotypes.label: Hypertension, dyslipidemia, gout, stroke
phenotypes.description: Atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease with arterial pathology (carotid stenosis/occlusion, cerebral atherosclerosis) appears alongside major vascular risk factors: essential hypertension, mixed dyslipidemia/hypertriglyceridemia, impaired glucose tolerance, and gout. Stroke events and sequelae (hemiparesis, dysarthria) are prominent, with related findings such as heart murmur also present. Within this population it is more common in older adults and in men.

phenotypes.label: Degenerative retinal and vitreous disease
phenotypes.description: Predominantly age-related ocular degeneration: age-related macular degeneration (nonexudative and exudative), vitreous degeneration/opacities and posterior vitreous detachment, epiretinal membrane, and other retinal disorders. Associated findings include glaucoma suspect, optic nerve abnormalities, dry eye, and eyelid dermatochalasis, reflecting an older-skewing group.

phenotypes.label: Anxiety, depression, and insomnia
phenotypes.description: An anxiety–depression spectrum phenotype marked by generalized anxiety disorder and recurrent major depressive disorder, with frequent co-occurrence of primary/psychophysiologic insomnia and panic or acute stress reactions. Adjustment disorder with anxious mood and ADHD also appear, reflecting broader mood, anxiety, and sleep disturbance. This captures patients whose primary burden is mood and anxiety disorders with sleep dysregulation.

phenotypes.label: IBD with malabsorption and perianal disease
phenotypes.description: Pattern centers on inflammatory bowel disease, especially Crohn’s, with intestinal obstruction, fistulas, perianal pain/abscesses, and aphthous ulcers. Frequent malabsorption and nutritional deficiencies (B12/cobalamin, vitamin D, thiamine, zinc) appear alongside related diagnoses such as celiac disease and enteropathic arthritis, reflecting extraintestinal involvement.

phenotypes.label: Primary care and dental baseline
phenotypes.description: General ambulatory pattern with common cardiometabolic conditions (essential hypertension, mixed hyperlipidemia, obesity), dental caries/periodontal disease, and upper respiratory infections with cough and sinusitis. Sexual health and STI diagnoses and routine depression screening also appear. This reflects a broad primary‑care baseline rather than a specific disease phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Coronary artery disease and ischemia
phenotypes.description: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease pattern with coronary and peripheral artery disease. Patients present with chest pain, syncope/collapse, and acute myocardial infarction, with coexisting dyslipidemia and abnormal glucose/Type 1 diabetes codes. This captures ischemic heart disease burden and related cardiovascular symptoms.

phenotypes.label: Anxiety and depressive disorders
phenotypes.description: Predominant anxiety and depressive disorders with associated somatic and functional complaints such as fatigue, hyperhidrosis, jaw/TMJ pain, GERD, IBS‑C, and sinus symptoms. Adjustment reactions and mood swings appear alongside incidental minor injuries and skin infections, reflecting a stress‑related, symptom‑burdened profile rather than a single organ disease.

phenotypes.label: Multiple sclerosis and spinal cord disease
phenotypes.description: Neurologic disorders with demyelinating and spinal cord involvement, including multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica, cervical myelopathy, and sequelae of spinal cord injury. Patients have paresthesias, muscle weakness and spasm, ataxia, foot drop, and gait impairment, often with neurogenic bladder or urge incontinence and, in some cases, paraplegia with wheelchair dependence.

phenotypes.label: Seizures with intracranial pathology
phenotypes.description: This pattern centers on epilepsy and seizure presentations, including partial seizures, status epilepticus, and seizure‑related loss of consciousness. It co-occurs with focal neurologic deficits and cognitive changes (aphasia, amnesia, slurred speech, altered mental status) and with structural/vascular brain disease such as aneurysm, subarachnoid hemorrhage, arteriovenous malformation, cerebral edema, hydrocephalus, head injury, and encephalitis. Psychogenic non-epileptic events and conversion symptoms also appear, reflecting the differential for convulsive episodes.

phenotypes.label: Rheumatoid and osteoarthritis cluster
phenotypes.description: Inflammatory arthritis centered on rheumatoid arthritis with prominent hand/wrist involvement and synovitis/tenosynovitis. Co-occurs with osteoarthritis, regional joint pains, and osteoporotic fractures, with extra‑articular autoimmune features such as Sjögren’s and episcleritis. This pattern is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Mixed clinical themes
phenotypes.description: The leading conditions are disparate—attention-deficit symptoms and mood findings, acute respiratory infections with cough and pharyngitis, musculoskeletal foot problems, dermatologic and eye disorders, and scattered endocrine and genitourinary findings. This reflects a blend of unrelated presentations rather than a single coherent disease phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Cervical radiculopathy and spondylosis
phenotypes.description: Degenerative cervical spine disease with nerve root involvement. Patients present with neck pain radiating to the arms, paresthesias or numbness, and conditions such as cervical spondylosis, disc degeneration or displacement, spinal stenosis, and sometimes cervical myelopathy; upper-limb mononeuropathies (e.g., ulnar lesion, brachial neuritis) are also represented.

phenotypes.label: Thyroid disease with musculoskeletal pain
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on hyperthyroidism and Graves disease (thyrotoxicosis, toxic diffuse goiter, exophthalmos) with palpitations. Co‑occurring musculoskeletal complaints (limb pain, myopathy, arthropathy) and reflux/asthma symptoms feature prominently, and the burden skews female with some gynecologic diagnoses present.

phenotypes.label: Postoperative care and complications
phenotypes.description: Conditions indicating postoperative and postprocedural states with procedure-related complications such as persistent postoperative pain, wound dehiscence, and postprocedural infection. The pattern is enriched for neurosurgical and orthopedic contexts, including brain neoplasms with hydrocephalus or midline shift and musculoskeletal injuries like rotator cuff tears and tibia/fibula or ankle fractures, reflecting post-surgical follow-up and sequelae.

phenotypes.label: HIV with STI and opportunistic infections
phenotypes.description: Human immunodeficiency virus infection accompanied by a high burden of sexually transmitted infections (genital herpes, gonorrhea, HPV/condyloma). Opportunistic and mucocutaneous infections such as oral candidiasis and herpes zoster, and tuberculin test reactions, are common, reflecting HIV-related infectious morbidity.

phenotypes.label: Thyroid/parathyroid disorders with calcium imbalance
phenotypes.description: Cluster of thyroid and parathyroid disorders including goiter, thyroid nodules and carcinoma, and postoperative hypothyroidism, with associated neck mass and voice changes (dysphonia, vocal cord paralysis). Prominent calcium–parathyroid axis findings (primary hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia/hypocalcemia) and vitamin D deficiency point to metabolic involvement. This pattern is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Allergic rhinitis with asthma and sinusitis
phenotypes.description: Atopic airway disease featuring allergic rhinitis (seasonal/pollen, animal dander) with chronic rhinosinusitis, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, turbinate hypertrophy, and loss of smell, together with asthma from intermittent to persistent with exacerbations. Allergic conjunctivitis and eustachian tube dysfunction commonly accompany this cluster. Within this cohort, it is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Postmenopausal osteoporosis and fractures
phenotypes.description: Metabolic bone disease centered on osteoporosis/osteopenia with vitamin D deficiency and osteoporotic fractures, often vertebral or appendicular. The pattern aligns with menopause and postmenopausal state with vasomotor and urogenital symptoms and is predominantly in older women. Some records also include breast-related conditions and mitral valve prolapse, but the core is postmenopausal bone loss.

phenotypes.label: Acute pain, injury, and infection
phenotypes.description: Acute presentations dominated by non‑specific pain, musculoskeletal injury/fracture, and respiratory viral illness (including COVID‑19) with fever, sore throat, and wheezing. This reflects symptom‑driven, short‑term complaints rather than chronic disease management.

phenotypes.label: Mixed ENT and pelvic floor disorders
phenotypes.description: The leading conditions span unrelated systems: otologic complaints with hearing loss and chronic laryngitis alongside lower urinary tract symptoms and female pelvic organ prolapse (cystocele, rectocele). Additional scattered benign issues (alopecia, lipoma, hordeolum, fecal impaction) further indicate no single unifying condition. Overall this combines multiple primary‑care problems rather than one coherent phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Psoriatic arthritis and enthesitis
phenotypes.description: Psoriatic disease with musculoskeletal involvement, including psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, enthesitis, and dactylitis. Prominent are shoulder and hand/wrist tendon and joint disorders, chronic pain, and elevated inflammatory markers, with coexisting degenerative changes such as osteoarthritis and spondylosis. Occasional upper-limb fractures appear, but the dominant pattern is an inflammatory spondyloarthropathy.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes predominates with poor control and complications including neuropathy, peripheral nerve disorders, and diabetic kidney disease. It clusters with metabolic comorbidities—hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity/metabolic syndrome—and skin/soft‑tissue conditions such as tinea pedis, onychomycosis, and paronychia. Patients skew older.

phenotypes.label: Hand and foot arthritis and pain
phenotypes.description: Peripheral joint disorders centered on the ankles, feet, hands, and fingers, with prominent arthralgia, synovitis, and joint stiffness. The pattern spans degenerative osteoarthritis and inflammatory arthropathies (including rheumatoid arthritis), often accompanied by hallux valgus, ankle instability/effusion, and focal hand–foot pain.

phenotypes.label: Lower gastrointestinal and anorectal disorders
phenotypes.description: Lower GI and anorectal conditions predominate, including hemorrhoids (internal/external) with rectal bleeding and anal fissure/pain, alongside irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea, bloating, and altered bowel habits. Colitis and diverticular disease are present, with frequent benign colorectal neoplasms and other digestive symptoms.

phenotypes.label: Migraine and headache disorders
phenotypes.description: Migraine-centered headache spectrum including migraine with and without aura, chronic/refractory subtypes, status migrainosus, and tension-type headache. Associated pain and neurogenic features appear, such as trigeminal/atypical facial pain, cervico-occipital neuralgia, myofascial and neck pain, dizziness/dysautonomia, and benign intracranial hypertension with transient visual loss. This pattern is more common in females and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Injection drug use complications
phenotypes.description: Pattern of opioid and other substance use disorders accompanied by injection-related skin and soft tissue infections (cellulitis/abscesses, often MRSA/MSSA), hepatitis C, dental infections, and trauma/poisonings. This profile appears more often in men and skews toward younger adults.

phenotypes.label: Lymphoma plus otologic and GI disorders
phenotypes.description: Hematologic malignancies (non‑Hodgkin subtypes with lymphadenopathy, neutropenia, SIRS, and vascular device complications) are intermingled with unrelated otologic problems (hearing loss, tinnitus) and common gastrointestinal conditions (GERD, gastric ulcer, pancreatic/pseudocyst), plus incidental musculoskeletal and renal findings. The mix spans distinct body systems and does not form a single clinical syndrome.

phenotypes.label: Gastrointestinal bleeding with iron-deficiency anemia
phenotypes.description: Gastrointestinal blood loss with iron‑deficiency anemia, with melena and rectal hemorrhage prominent. Etiologies and comorbid findings include diverticulosis, chronic gastritis/peptic ulcer disease, and ulcerative colitis with urgency, proctitis, and pouchitis, plus colonic adenomas/polyps that may bleed. Primary sclerosing cholangitis appears, aligning with ulcerative colitis.

phenotypes.label: Ocular surface and corneal disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of ocular surface and anterior segment disease: tear film insufficiency/dry eye, blepharitis and meibomian gland dysfunction, and keratoconjunctivitis sicca in contexts such as Sjögren’s syndrome or graft‑versus‑host disease. It also features corneal dystrophies and scarring, cataract with pseudophakia, eyelid malposition (ptosis/ectropion), and chronic angle‑closure glaucoma with associated ocular pain and visual disturbance.

phenotypes.label: CKD/ESRD with complications
phenotypes.description: Spectrum of chronic kidney disease from stage 2–5 and end‑stage renal disease, often attributed to hypertensive or diabetic nephropathy. Complications include anemia of CKD, hyperkalemia, proteinuria, mineral–bone disorders (secondary hyperparathyroidism and phosphorus/magnesium abnormalities), acute kidney injury episodes, dialysis access/device complications, and kidney transplant status. This pattern skews older and is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Bipolar spectrum with insomnia/anxiety
phenotypes.description: Psychiatric profile centered on bipolar disorder and insomnia, with accompanying mood and anxiety disorders. Comorbidities include obsessive–compulsive disorder, post‑traumatic stress disorder, and borderline personality disorder, with codes spanning hypomanic, depressive, and remitted bipolar episodes. Injury-related presentations also co-occur.

phenotypes.label: Cardiometabolic and lymphoid malignancy mix
phenotypes.description: This cluster blends common cardiometabolic and age-associated gastrointestinal conditions (hypercholesterolemia, impaired fasting glucose, hypertension, colon polyps, diverticulosis/diverticulitis, GERD) with a separate set of lymphoid hematologic disorders (chronic lymphocytic leukemia, lymphocytosis, leukemia, autoimmune hemolytic anemia). These represent unrelated clinical themes combined in one topic rather than a single phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Parkinsonism with cognitive and autonomic features
phenotypes.description: Motor parkinsonism features (resting tremor, bradykinesia, dysarthria/dysphagia, gait instability with falls) cluster with non-motor symptoms such as orthostatic hypotension, constipation, sialorrhea, REM sleep behavior disorder, and visual hallucinations. Cognitive impairment and dementia suggest Parkinson’s disease dementia or Lewy body disease within this group.

phenotypes.label: Paraproteinemia-associated neuropathy and amyloidosis
phenotypes.description: Plasma cell dyscrasias (MGUS, multiple myeloma, Waldenström) presenting with peripheral neuropathy, including idiopathic/inflammatory variants, and associated amyloidosis and hypogammaglobulinemia. Anemia and other hematologic abnormalities are common, with chronic pain and fatigue also appearing.

phenotypes.label: COPD with tobacco use and exacerbations
phenotypes.description: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and emphysema, frequently with acute exacerbations and dyspnea, strongly associated with active tobacco use. Comorbid conditions include GERD, anxiety/insomnia, and chronic pain, with hypertension and obesity as background risks. Bipolar spectrum diagnoses appear in a subset.

phenotypes.label: Acute cardiopulmonary symptoms
phenotypes.description: Cluster of acute cardiopulmonary complaints centered on dyspnea, palpitations, cough, chest pain, dizziness, and fatigue. Records often include abnormal breathing and ECG abnormalities, with asthma and GERD appearing as adjacent diagnoses. Overall this reflects nonspecific cardiorespiratory symptom presentations across the cohort.

phenotypes.label: Low back pain and spondyloarthritis
phenotypes.description: Chronic axial musculoskeletal pain dominated by low back pain, with spine and sacroiliac joint disorders and ankylosing spondylitis. Associated features include enthesitis and uveitis, with shoulder and neck pain also present, consistent with an axial spondyloarthritis spectrum.

phenotypes.label: Cancer with lung nodules and masses
phenotypes.description: Malignant neoplasms across multiple primary sites with associated mass/lump findings and abnormal thoracic imaging, including solitary pulmonary nodules and cough. Imaging-driven incidental findings (e.g., aortic atherosclerosis, renal cysts), postoperative state, and medical care complications commonly co-occur, consistent with cancer diagnosis and surveillance coding.

phenotypes.label: Age-related ocular disorders with presbycusis
phenotypes.description: Age-related eye conditions dominate: refractive errors (myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism) with presbyopia, cataracts (including nuclear), ocular hypertension, and primary open-angle glaucoma. Sensorineural hearing loss, including presbycusis and Ménière’s disease, co-occurs, indicating a broader age-associated sensory decline and a skew toward older adults.

phenotypes.label: Thoracic imaging abnormalities and lung cancer
phenotypes.description: Abnormal chest imaging with atelectasis, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, pneumonia, bronchiectasis, emphysema, and lung nodules. Frequent co-occurrence of primary lung cancer with nodal and bone metastases, cancer-related pain, anemia, and severe protein-calorie malnutrition indicates substantial thoracic malignancy burden within a pulmonary disease context.

phenotypes.label: Prediabetes and metabolic risk
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on prediabetes and dysglycemia, with co‑occurring obesity, essential hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Vitamin D deficiency and generic abnormal chemistry findings appear alongside, reflecting a cardiometabolic risk profile rather than acute illness.

phenotypes.label: Allergic dermatoses and urticaria-angioedema
phenotypes.description: Cluster of allergic and atopic skin disease with pruritic eruptions, atopic/contact dermatitis, multiple urticaria subtypes, and angioedema. Many patients show an atopic diathesis with asthma and cough, with occasional immune dysregulation such as mast‑cell disease within this pattern.

phenotypes.label: Decompensated cirrhosis and portal hypertension
phenotypes.description: Advanced chronic liver disease characterized by portal hypertension and decompensation: ascites, esophageal/gastric varices, splenomegaly with thrombocytopenia/pancytopenia, abnormal liver tests, and hepatic failure/encephalopathy (asterixis, hepatic coma). Etiologies and related hepatobiliary conditions include alcoholic and nonalcoholic cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis C, nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, portal vein thrombosis, and hepatic lesions/mass.

phenotypes.label: Gynecologic cancers and hereditary predisposition
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on gynecologic malignancies—ovarian, endometrial, and uterine cancer—with abdominal/pelvic masses and documented genetic cancer susceptibility. Accompanying conditions include anemia, fatigue, constipation, GERD, and postoperative or device-related issues such as peritoneal adhesions and central line bloodstream infection. This pattern predominantly reflects female patients with hereditary risk and active abdominal–pelvic oncologic disease.

phenotypes.label: Acute cardiopulmonary and GI symptoms
phenotypes.description: Nonspecific acute presentations with dyspnea and chest pain with wheeze, alongside nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and abdominal pain. Also includes generalized pain, bleeding, and anxiety, reflecting common symptom-driven encounters rather than a single disease process.

phenotypes.label: Lumbar spine pain with radiculopathy
phenotypes.description: Degenerative lumbar spine disorders with low back pain and radicular symptoms. Findings include lumbar spondylosis, intervertebral disc degeneration or herniation, spinal stenosis, sciatica/lumbosacral radiculopathy, and chronic pain syndromes, with occasional sacroiliac or thoracic involvement. Patients present with recurrent axial pain and nerve root irritation features.

phenotypes.label: Cardiac arrhythmias and structural heart disease
phenotypes.description: Coherent cluster of atrial fibrillation/flutter, supraventricular and ventricular ectopy, bradyarrhythmias and conduction disease, alongside structural heart conditions including valvular disorders, cardiomegaly, and aortic aneurysm/ectasia. This reflects patients with cardiac rhythm disturbances and underlying structural heart disease; it skews older and is somewhat more common in men.

phenotypes.label: Chronic venous insufficiency with stasis ulcers
phenotypes.description: Lower-extremity venous disease with varicose veins and chronic venous insufficiency causing edema, limb pain, lymphedema, and superficial phlebitis. Complications include venous stasis changes with chronic ankle/lower-leg ulcers, open wounds, cellulitis, and postthrombotic syndrome.

phenotypes.label: Sleep-disordered breathing with obesity
phenotypes.description: Cluster of sleep-disordered breathing centered on obstructive sleep apnea with snoring, hypersomnia, insomnia, parasomnias, and periodic limb movement/restless legs. Strong association with obesity, including morbid obesity and bariatric surgery-related malabsorption, and codes for device dependence consistent with positive airway pressure use.

phenotypes.label: Major depression and anxiety
phenotypes.description: Mood disorders centered on major depressive episodes, including severe and psychotic-feature variants, with co-occurring generalized anxiety. Somatic symptoms such as GERD, constipation, dizziness, chest pain, and respiratory or urinary complaints commonly accompany these visits.

phenotypes.label: Acute abdominal pain and GI upset
phenotypes.description: Abdominal pain (generalized and localized), epigastric pain, nausea/vomiting, and diarrhea predominate, often with dehydration or fever. This reflects acute gastrointestinal presentations such as gastroenteritis, gastritis/peptic ulcer disease, biliary colic/cholecystitis, and inflammatory bowel disease flares. Within the cohort it skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Type 1 diabetes, acute decompensation
phenotypes.description: Type 1 diabetes with acute metabolic crises characterized by hyperglycemia/diabetic ketoacidosis or hypoglycemia, dehydration, acidosis, and electrolyte abnormalities (hyponatremia, hypokalemia), often with hypotension and acute kidney injury. Infectious precipitants and systemic inflammation (pyelonephritis, pneumonia, sepsis/SIRS) are common, with diabetic autonomic complications such as gastroparesis and neuropathy also noted; some episodes include respiratory failure.

phenotypes.label: Pregnancy and obstetric complications
phenotypes.description: Obstetric conditions centered on pregnancy and its complications, including high‑risk pregnancy, trimester-specific gestational ages, and peripartum findings such as placenta previa, threatened preterm labor, fetal growth restriction, and postpartum issues. It reflects the full obstetric course with maternal factors like obesity and anemia, twin gestation, cervical incompetence, breech presentation, and placental disorders. This cluster is concentrated in younger female patients.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic foot disease and retinopathy
phenotypes.description: Advanced diabetes with peripheral arterial disease, neuropathy, and diabetic foot ulcers complicated by cellulitis, osteomyelitis, and amputation. Microvascular eye disease is prominent (proliferative retinopathy, macular edema, vitreous hemorrhage) with vision loss; this pattern is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: PTSD, hearing loss, dental disease
phenotypes.description: This blends PTSD and depressive disorders with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus, extensive dental disease (caries, gingivitis, calculus), and musculoskeletal pain involving the foot/hip/back including pes planus and bursitis. There is no single unifying clinical process, reflecting co‑occurring mental health, ENT, dental, and musculoskeletal problems.

phenotypes.label: Chronic comorbidity catch-all with smoking
phenotypes.description: Hypertension, obesity, GERD, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes appear alongside common primary‑care symptoms such as chest pain, cough, dizziness, headache, and low back pain. Nicotine dependence and asthma suggest a smoking‑related respiratory burden layered onto these chronic conditions. Overall this represents a general chronic comorbidity baseline.

phenotypes.label: Pituitary adenoma and endocrine dysfunction
phenotypes.description: Cluster of pituitary disorders with hormonal excess and deficiency. Features include pituitary adenomas/prolactinoma with hyperprolactinemia, acromegaly, Cushing’s disease, and diabetes insipidus, alongside hypopituitarism/panhypopituitarism. Secondary endocrine effects such as testicular hypofunction and adrenal cortical hypofunction are common in this pattern.

phenotypes.label: Systemic sclerosis with esophageal dysmotility
phenotypes.description: Connective tissue disease dominated by systemic sclerosis features with prominent esophageal involvement (dysphagia, GERD, esophagitis, achalasia). Pulmonary manifestations are common, including interstitial lung disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, hypoxemia, and cor pulmonale, often alongside Raynaud’s and CREST/overlap syndromes.

phenotypes.label: Hepatobiliary disease with dyspepsia
phenotypes.description: Hepatobiliary and upper GI conditions predominate, including nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, gallstones/cholecystitis, gastritis/functional dyspepsia, and GERD with epigastric pain. The cluster also includes chronic viral hepatitis and bilirubin metabolism disorders with occasional biliary dilation, reflecting a biliary–liver axis phenotype that often coexists with obesity.

phenotypes.label: Psychosis with substance use and injury
phenotypes.description: Severe psychotic illness featuring schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorders with hallucinations, delusions, and crisis presentations. Prominent nicotine and polysubstance use accompany suicidal ideation, intentional poisoning, and traumatic injuries (lacerations, abrasions). Within the cohort this cluster is more common in males and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Breast cancer and imaging findings
phenotypes.description: Breast conditions centered on female breast malignancy with related diagnostic findings. Features include breast lumps, abnormal mammography with microcalcifications, DCIS/LCIS, ER‑positive tumors, and benign breast disease such as fibrocystic change. Associated conditions include lymphedema, radiation dermatitis, and postoperative complications; this pattern is predominantly in women and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Sun damage and pigmented lesions
phenotypes.description: Cutaneous conditions centered on actinic damage and pigmented lesions: actinic and seborrheic keratoses, melanocytic/dysplastic nevi, pigment disorders, scars, and skin cancers (notably basal cell, occasional melanoma). The pattern reflects chronic photodamage and is more common in older adults.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic foot, neuropathy, and infections
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with peripheral neuropathy, peripheral vascular disease, and prominent foot complications—onychomycosis, ingrown nails, toe pain, cellulitis, and foot infection—often with hyperglycemia. Renal involvement (proteinuria) and severe lower-extremity sequelae, including post‑amputation status, also appear. This pattern is more common in men and increases with age.

phenotypes.label: Knee osteoarthritis and meniscal disorders
phenotypes.description: Degenerative knee disease centered on osteoarthritis with bilateral knee pain, effusion, and meniscal tears/derangements. Related findings include patellofemoral disorders, hip osteoarthritis, and occasional prosthetic joint complications.

phenotypes.label: Mixed clinical themes
phenotypes.description: The leading conditions combine behavioral health diagnoses (posttraumatic stress disorder, recurrent major depressive disorder, panic disorders) with acute upper respiratory and ear infections (pharyngitis, otitis media, bronchitis, sinusitis), plus scattered dental, skin/soft tissue, and minor injury problems. These represent unrelated clinical issues rather than a single phenotype, so there is no unifying clinical pathway.

phenotypes.label: Retinal disorders and visual impairment
phenotypes.description: Ophthalmic disease centered on retinal pathology, visual disturbance, and vision loss, including retinal detachment, retinal vein occlusions with macular edema, epiretinal membrane, retinoschisis, and cystoid macular degeneration. Ocular inflammatory conditions (iridocyclitis/uveitis, scleritis, chorioretinitis) and cataract/secondary cataract with ocular hypertension are common, with frequent visual field defects and blindness. Systemic associations such as sarcoidosis and sickle cell disease appear among affected patients.

phenotypes.label: Gynecologic disorders with pelvic pain
phenotypes.description: Female reproductive tract conditions centered on pelvic pain, ovarian cysts, uterine leiomyomas, endometriosis, dysmenorrhea with irregular or heavy menses, vaginitis, dyspareunia, and anovulatory infertility; includes acute entities such as pelvic inflammatory disease, adnexal torsion, and ectopic pregnancy. Predominantly seen in women of reproductive age.

phenotypes.label: Depression and anxiety spectrum
phenotypes.description: Predominantly depressive and anxiety disorders, including recurrent major depression, dysthymia, and mixed anxiety–depressive states, with frequent insomnia. Comorbidities include tobacco dependence, eating disorders, malaise, and musculoskeletal pain, reflecting somatic symptoms often accompanying mood and anxiety conditions.

phenotypes.label: Shoulder girdle pain with PMR/GCA
phenotypes.description: Cluster of shoulder osteoarthritis and shoulder pain/impingement with accompanying carpal tunnel syndrome and trigger finger, plus a polymyalgia rheumatica/giant cell arteritis signal (raised ESR, temporal arteritis). This reflects upper-limb degenerative disease and PMR/GCA-related shoulder girdle pain, and it skews to older adults.

phenotypes.label: Cardiometabolic comorbidity baseline
phenotypes.description: Common cardiometabolic profile with essential hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, and obesity. Vascular disease and related chronic conditions such as coronary atherosclerosis, GERD, and vitamin D deficiency often appear alongside. Within the cohort this pattern skews toward older adults and men.

phenotypes.label: ADHD with anxiety and mood disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions centered on attention‑deficit/hyperactivity disorder with comorbid anxiety, depression, insomnia, and episodes of suicidality; some cases include mania, psychosis, or hallucinations. Autism spectrum, tic, and impulse‑control disorders co-occur, indicating a broader behavioral spectrum that skews younger within the cohort.

phenotypes.label: Advanced liver disease and transplant sequelae
phenotypes.description: Advanced liver disease with liver transplantation and hepatobiliary complications is prominent, including biliary obstruction, hepatocellular carcinoma, hemochromatosis, hepatorenal syndrome, and postoperative state. Abdominal wall, umbilical, and incisional hernias co-occur with anemia, immune dysfunction/immunodeficiency, and severe infections such as viral pneumonia, sepsis, and acute respiratory distress.

phenotypes.label: Colorectal cancer with postoperative complications
phenotypes.description: Pattern of colorectal malignancy with prior abdominal surgery and ostomy status. Conditions include postoperative complications such as adhesions with obstruction, stoma disorder or malfunction, and wound dehiscence, with accompanying gastrointestinal complaints. The frequent documentation of acquired absence of organ reflects prior resection (e.g., colectomy/proctectomy).

phenotypes.label: Prostate disease and male LUTS
phenotypes.description: Male urologic disease centered on the prostate: benign prostatic hyperplasia with or without outlet obstruction, elevated PSA and prostate cancer, with lower urinary tract symptoms (nocturia, frequency, poor stream). Erectile dysfunction, urinary incontinence, prostatitis, urinary obstruction, and occasional radiation proctitis or catheter-related issues also appear; the pattern skews strongly male and older.

phenotypes.label: Venous thromboembolism and thrombophilia
phenotypes.description: Acute and chronic venous thromboembolism, notably pulmonary embolism and lower‑extremity DVT, presenting with dyspnea, chest pain, limb swelling, and occasionally acute cor pulmonale. Hypercoagulable states and inherited thrombophilias (e.g., antiphospholipid syndrome, Factor V Leiden) are prominent, with abnormal coagulation findings and related thrombotic complications.

phenotypes.label: Hashimoto thyroiditis with hypothyroidism
phenotypes.description: Autoimmune thyroid disease with Hashimoto thyroiditis and hypothyroidism, often with thyroid atrophy/goiter and abnormal thyroid function. Accompanied by fatigue and alopecia areata; patients skew older and female, with menopausal and post‑hysterectomy findings common.

phenotypes.label: Hematuria, cystitis, and urolithiasis
phenotypes.description: Urologic cluster centered on hematuria, dysuria, and lower urinary tract symptoms with frequent cystitis/UTI and bladder disorders. Prominent stone disease (kidney and ureteral calculi) with obstructive sequelae such as hydronephrosis and retention is present, and a subset reflects bladder neoplasia.

phenotypes.label: Ischemic heart disease with heart failure
phenotypes.description: Coronary atherosclerosis and ischemic cardiomyopathy with prior myocardial infarction and angina, often with prior coronary bypass, dominate this cluster. It features chronic systolic/diastolic heart failure with pulmonary hypertension and episodes of decompensation including respiratory failure, dyspnea, and chest pain, with left ventricular dysfunction and conduction disease reflected. Within the cohort it skews older and more often male.

phenotypes.label: Alcohol use disorders and complications
phenotypes.description: Alcohol use disorders—abuse, dependence, intoxication, and withdrawal—with complications including alcoholic gastritis, hematemesis, acute and chronic pancreatitis, toxic encephalopathy, malnutrition, and neuropathy. Trauma and injury patterns (rib fracture, head injury, hemothorax) and co-occurring substance use (nicotine, cannabis, cocaine) are prominent. Within the cohort this pattern is more common in men and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with asthma
phenotypes.description: Patients with type 2 diabetes co-occurring with asthma, including wheeze and acute exacerbations. Gastroesophageal reflux, depressive symptoms and eating disorders, and autoimmune/inflammatory complaints are common, with some chronic diarrhea. Additional findings include carpal tunnel syndrome, myopia, benign polyps, biliary calculi, and chest wall tenderness.

phenotypes.label: Uncontrolled diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes marked by severe hyperglycemia and hyperosmolar crises, with documented diabetic complications such as neuropathy. Cardiometabolic comorbidities including hypertension and mixed hyperlipidemia are common. This pattern skews male.

phenotypes.label: Severe obesity with insulin resistance
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on severe/morbid obesity with insulin resistance, prediabetes, and abnormal glucose. Associated metabolic comorbidities include obstructive sleep apnea and fatty liver disease, with occasional gestational diabetes in reproductive-age patients. This reflects a metabolic-syndrome spectrum with high adiposity burden.

phenotypes.label: Obesity with diabetic kidney disease
phenotypes.description: Distinct metabolic phenotype in GLP-1 RA users dominated by severe obesity with diabetic kidney disease, reflected by proteinuria and related renal diagnoses. Co-occurring metabolic features include hypertriglyceridemia, dyslipidemia, and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.

phenotypes.label: OSA with metabolic syndrome
phenotypes.description: Obstructive sleep apnea clustered with severe obesity and cardiometabolic comorbidities (hypertension, hyperlipidemia), alongside hypothyroidism and GERD. Extreme obesity with alveolar hypoventilation and urogynecologic symptoms (mixed urinary incontinence, postmenopausal bleeding) also appear, reflecting an obesity-related symptom burden in this subgroup.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic microvascular complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with microvascular complications: diabetic neuropathy (including autonomic), retinopathy with macular edema, and diabetic kidney disease, with diabetic foot changes such as ulcers and calluses. This pattern also includes hypoglycemia episodes and skews to older and male patients within the subgroup.

phenotypes.label: Uncomplicated type 2 diabetes
phenotypes.description: This foreground pattern for GLP‑1 RA users is dominated by uncomplicated type 2 diabetes, with common cardiometabolic comorbidities such as hypertension and hyperlipidemia appearing alongside minor incidental conditions. Within this subgroup it is relatively more common in males and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Obesity, diabetes, and GI symptoms
phenotypes.description: Severe obesity and diabetes with prominent gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation) and reflux. Comorbidities include sleep apnea, hypertension, fatty liver disease and gallstones, with occasional pancreatitis and endocrine features (hypothyroidism, goiter) and hypoglycemia; more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Among GLP‑1 receptor agonist users, this pattern centers on type 2 diabetes—often insulin‑treated and described as well controlled—with microvascular complications including retinopathy, peripheral neuropathy, and microalbuminuria. Glycemic abnormalities (hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia) are frequent, alongside metabolic and cardiovascular comorbidities such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperuricemia, and early renal impairment. Features like numbness in the feet and trigger finger further reflect diabetic neuropathy and tendon involvement.

phenotypes.label: Severe obesity and metabolic syndrome
phenotypes.description: Severe obesity with clustered metabolic comorbidities, including metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, GERD, and mild asthma. Nutritional deficiencies and related dermatologic or infectious issues (vitamin D and iron deficiency, intertrigo, candidiasis) are frequent, with features of androgen excess/ovulatory dysfunction (PCOS, hirsutism) and occasional post-surgical malabsorption. Within this subgroup the pattern skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Degenerative lumbar spine with radiculopathy
phenotypes.description: Chronic low back pain and sciatica centered on lumbar radiculopathy with degenerative spine disease. The pattern includes lumbar spondylosis, disc degeneration, spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication, and post-laminectomy syndrome, with frequent chronic pain syndrome and fibromyalgia features.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic neuropathy and peripheral angiopathy
phenotypes.description: Advanced type 2 diabetes with peripheral neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease, with diabetic foot complications: toe wounds/ulcers, onychomycosis and nail dystrophy, cellulitis, and prior toe or limb amputation. Hypertension, mixed hyperlipidemia, and atherosclerotic disease are frequent comorbidities. Within this subgroup it is more common in older men.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic nephropathy with microvascular complications
phenotypes.description: Among GLP-1 RA users, this reflects diabetic kidney disease (stages 2–4) with proteinuria and anemia of CKD, often with hyperkalemia and intermittent acute kidney injury. It co-occurs with diabetic neuropathies and retinopathy alongside hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gout/hyperuricemia. Within this subgroup it skews older and more often male.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Advanced type 2 diabetes with metabolic syndrome features (hyperlipidemia, hypertension, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea) and microvascular complications including neuropathy, retinopathy, albuminuria, and renal insufficiency. Also notable for macrovascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis, peripheral arterial disease with claudication) and diabetic gastroparesis and hypoglycemia, consistent with long‑standing, complicated disease.

phenotypes.label: Coronary atherosclerosis with diabetic retinopathy
phenotypes.description: Patients with coronary atherosclerosis and angina in the setting of long‑standing hypertension and hyperlipidemia; some have prior coronary bypass grafts. Ocular complications of diabetes and hypertension are prominent, including nonproliferative and hypertensive retinopathy, retinal hemorrhage, and cataracts. Obesity and diabetic neurologic complications are present, and within this subgroup the pattern skews older and male.

phenotypes.label: SGLT2i uncontrolled T2DM with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with poor control, featuring hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, and diabetic complications including retinopathy, neuropathy, and foot problems; many are coded as insulin-treated. Co-occurring conditions include genital and foot infections, severe obesity, and atherosclerotic disease such as stable angina and arterial occlusion.

phenotypes.label: SGLT2i diabetic CKD with complications
phenotypes.description: Within the SGLT2 inhibitor cohort, this pattern reflects chronic kidney disease—predominantly stage 3 (3A/3B)—driven by type 2 diabetes and hypertension, with occasional progression to stage 4 or acute kidney injury. Associated complications include hyperkalemia, anemia of CKD, secondary hyperparathyroidism, hematuria, and renal cysts, with comorbid gout/hyperuricemia and cardiorenal disease (hypertensive heart disease, systolic heart failure). It skews toward older patients.

phenotypes.label: SGLT2i diabetic ocular disease
phenotypes.description: Among SGLT2i users, this reflects type 2 diabetes with a heavy ophthalmic burden—senile and diabetic cataracts, glaucoma suspect, presbyopia, and refractive disorders. Cardiometabolic comorbidities are present but secondary, with occasional vascular findings (retinal vein occlusion, venous thromboembolism, abdominal aortic aneurysm) at lower frequency.

phenotypes.label: SGLT2i diabetic microvascular complications
phenotypes.description: Within SGLT2 inhibitor users, this phenotype reflects type 2 diabetes with microvascular complications, dominated by diabetic polyneuropathy and nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy, often with macular edema. Associated findings include foot numbness, hypertensive retinopathy, ocular hypertension/glaucoma, arteriosclerotic vascular disease, and onychomycosis.

phenotypes.label: Heart failure with atrial fibrillation
phenotypes.description: In SGLT2 inhibitor users, this captures a heart failure spectrum (systolic, diastolic, and combined) with hypertensive heart disease, cardiomyopathy, pulmonary hypertension, dyspnea, and prominent atrial fibrillation/flutter. Within this subgroup it skews older and is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: SGLT2i obesity, NAFLD, OSA phenotype
phenotypes.description: Obesity-related metabolic syndrome with type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, and fatty liver disease (NAFLD/NASH). Kidney involvement appears with renal impairment, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and electrolyte disturbances, and genital candidiasis is noted. Respiratory comorbidity including restrictive lung disease and secondary polycythemia aligns with sleep-disordered breathing in this group.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic neuropathy and foot disorders
phenotypes.description: Complications of type 2 diabetes centered on peripheral and autonomic neuropathy with ocular involvement, alongside prominent foot and nail disorders (onychomycosis, nail dystrophy, calluses, hammer toe) and occasional soft tissue infection. Cardiometabolic comorbidities (hypertension, hyperlipidemia) and GERD appear as coexisting conditions. Within SGLT2 inhibitor users, this pattern is relatively more common in men and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes without complications
phenotypes.description: Predominantly uncomplicated type 2 diabetes with common cardiometabolic comorbidities, including hyperlipidemia and essential hypertension. Additional associated conditions include colon polyps/diverticulosis and obstructive sleep apnea, with occasional benign adrenal adenomas and historic rheumatic valvular disease.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic kidney disease, CKD stage 3
phenotypes.description: Diabetic nephropathy characterized by albuminuria/proteinuria and chronic kidney disease (often stage 3). Hypertension, dyslipidemia, edema, nephrolithiasis or hydronephrosis appear alongside metabolic acidosis, hyperosmolarity, hypoalbuminemia, and anemia, reflecting renal and metabolic complications.

phenotypes.label: Diabetes neuropathy with glycosuria and candidiasis
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with prominent diabetic polyneuropathy, accompanied by foot and nail disorders (onychomycosis, ingrown nail, callosities/hammer toe) and cardiometabolic comorbidities. Distinctive features include glycosuria and genital candidiasis with vulvar pruritus; obstructive sleep apnea also appears.

phenotypes.label: Diabetes with foot ulcer and COPD
phenotypes.description: Pattern of type 2 diabetes with prominent diabetic foot disease (foot ulcer, foot/ankle degenerative changes). Respiratory comorbidity is notable, including emphysema/COPD, hypoxemia, and both obstructive and central sleep apnea. Psychiatric conditions (PTSD, depression/OCD) and male urogenital diagnoses (prostate carcinoma in situ, hypogonadism) also appear in this multimorbid cluster.

phenotypes.label: Shoulder disorders in diabetes
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with cardiometabolic comorbidity co-occurs with a concentrated burden of shoulder pathology: adhesive capsulitis, rotator cuff disease, biceps tendinitis, calcific tendinitis, and glenohumeral/AC osteoarthritis. Occasional balanitis and heart failure appear, but the defining pattern is painful and stiff shoulder disorders in patients with diabetes.

phenotypes.label: Decompensated heart failure with valvulopathy
phenotypes.description: Patients show decompensated heart failure with orthopnea, dyspnea, rales, hypervolemia, and episodes of diuresis, sometimes escalating to cardiogenic shock. Prominent associated findings include valvular regurgitation/stenosis (mitral, tricuspid, aortic), pulmonary hypertension, pericardial effusion, arrhythmias and conduction disease, and cardiomyopathy with syncope.

phenotypes.label: SGLT2i diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, obesity
phenotypes.description: SGLT2i subgroup with a cardiometabolic cluster: type 2 diabetes co-occurring with mixed hyperlipidemia and essential hypertension, often alongside morbid obesity. Intermittent hypoglycemia and atherogenic lipid abnormalities (elevated lipoprotein) appear, with occasional associated conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea and intertrigo.

phenotypes.label: Ischemic heart disease with PAD
phenotypes.description: Within the SGLT2 inhibitor subgroup, this captures advanced atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease: coronary artery disease with angina, prior infarction, ischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic systolic heart failure, alongside peripheral arterial disease and diabetic vascular complications. The burden is concentrated in older men in this subgroup.
